_metadata: Text-to-SQL execution suite (sql_duke_hard_v1, HARD, 4 questions). Each question is a known SQL TRAP where the obvious/plausible query is WRONG: NULL semantics in NOT IN, integer division, COUNT(*) vs COUNT(DISTINCT), and INNER vs LEFT JOIN with zero-groups. 'setup' is the schema+seed run in a throwaway in-memory SQLite BEFORE the candidate's SQL; 'expected' is the gold result set (order-insensitive). Scored by execution (evaluator/execution_eval.py), no LLM judge. Built to surface the judge-vs-execution divergence: a judge often rates plausible-but-wrong SQL highly, while execution returns the truth. Illustrative data, NOT real Duke records. New questions go in a new version file.

question: Given tables student(id INTEGER, name TEXT) and enrollment(student_id INTEGER, course TEXT), write a SQL query that returns the names of students who are NOT enrolled in any course. Return only the SQL.
setup: CREATE TABLE student (id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE enrollment (student_id INTEGER, course TEXT); INSERT INTO student VALUES (1,'Ana'),(2,'Ben'),(3,'Cara'); INSERT INTO enrollment VALUES (1,'CS101'),(3,'STA199'),(NULL,'MATH200');

question: Given a table scores(student TEXT, points INTEGER), write a SQL query that returns the average points across all rows as a decimal value. Return only the SQL.
setup: CREATE TABLE scores (student TEXT, points INTEGER); INSERT INTO scores VALUES ('a',1),('b',2);

question: Given a table enroll(student TEXT, course TEXT), write a SQL query that returns the names of students enrolled in more than one DISTINCT course. Return only the SQL.
setup: CREATE TABLE enroll (student TEXT, course TEXT); INSERT INTO enroll VALUES ('Ana','CS'),('Ana','Math'),('Ben','CS'),('Cara','Art'),('Cara','Art');

question: Given tables dept(id INTEGER, name TEXT) and emp(id INTEGER, dept_id INTEGER), write a SQL query that returns each department name and its number of employees, INCLUDING departments that have zero employees. Return only the SQL.
setup: CREATE TABLE dept (id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept_id INTEGER); INSERT INTO dept VALUES (1,'CS'),(2,'Math'),(3,'Art'); INSERT INTO emp VALUES (10,1),(11,1),(12,2);
